Chapter 1 of 5 // Interconnected Universe Hub

Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute

Blacksburg, Virginia //, Home of the Forgers & The Ironheads

The "Forger" Identity & The Ironheads

Nestled high in the Blue Ridge Mountains of Southwest Virginia, Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute (CPI) is the Commonwealth's premier land-grant polytechnic research university. Its students, faculty, and alumni are known worldwide as "The Forgers"—a tribute to the institute's 19th-century origins in metallurgy, heavy foundry engineering, and industrial mechanics.

Inside The Crucible, CPI's 65,000-seat concrete-and-steel football stadium, that blue-collar identity is personified by The Ironheads. Just as Buchanan University basketball is famous far and wide for The Pavilion Lunatics inside Buchanan Indoor Pavilion, CPI football is renowned across collegiate athletics for The Ironheads—the 20,000 fanatical students packed shoulder-to-shoulder onto the unpadded galvanized metal bleachers of the North End Zone (The Anvil). Wearing painted maroon-and-orange steel-mill hard hats and denim overalls, The Ironheads refuse to sit from kickoff to 0:00 and treat sideline decibel meters as a personal scoreboard.

Blacksburg & CPI Campus Gazetteer

Built from locally quarried grey-and-pink dolomitic limestone known universally as Ironstone, the CPI campus and the Town of Blacksburg operate as a living, interconnected grid where characters across eras and book series cross paths along the same quadrangles, halls, and transit corridors:

Commonwealth Green, Preston Hall, & Commonwealth Mall

Commonwealth Green is the vast central oval lawn at the heart of campus, ringed by neo-Gothic Ironstone academic halls and anchored on its northern rim by Preston Hall (the towering administrative headquarters housing the President's Office, Bursar, and 3,000-seat Preston Auditorium). Feeding the Green from the east is Commonwealth Mall, spanned by the iconic Ironstone arches of The Keystone Bridge (linking Keystone Hall to Pendleton Memorial Library). Before the dedicated multi-bay CPI Transit Center was constructed, every Blue Ridge Transit (BRT) route staged bumper-to-bumper along the curb of Commonwealth Mall beneath The Keystone Bridge in an infamous, diesel-choked nightmare—the exact curbside gauntlet where Erin rescued her twin brother John in November 2004.

Kincaid Hall, Callahan Hall, & The Engineering Quad

Along Commonwealth Mall sits Kincaid Hall (the bustling student union housing the Kincaid Ballroom, Kincaid Auditorium, and Second-Floor Lounge) and Callahan Hall (home to Services for Students with Disabilities / SSD). Directly northwest of Commonwealth Green rises the Engineering Quad—anchored by Faraday Hall (Electrical & Systems Engineering), Joule Hall (Mechanical & Materials Engineering), Kelvin Hall (Computer Science), and Archer Hall (General Lecture Hall)—while the Residential Quad is served by The Foundry, CPI's massive two-story rotunda dining hall.

Eleanor Bennett Commonwealth Hall ("The Old Lady") & Pepper Street

On campus, Eleanor Bennett Commonwealth Hall—known universally as Bennett Hall, "The Old Lady," or "The Old Lady on the Hill"—is a historic Ironstone residence hall whose Suite 214 serves as the sanctuary for Jordan Shawn Kelly, Aubrie, and the Group of 8 in The Aubrie Chronicles. Off campus, Progress Street NE is home to The Stardust Engine's Ironwood Collective, while the Pepper Street / Pepper Plaza corridor (anchored by Valu-Mart) houses Paige, Freddie, and Jessica at 105 Pepper Street.

The Crucible, The Furnace, & The I-81 Spine (Exits 118 & 98)

At the southern edge of campus stand The Crucible (65,000-seat football stadium) and The Furnace (10,000-seat basketball coliseum), both protected in perpetuity by the 1995 Ironhead Covenant. The university's reach extends down I-81 from the 8-level, 6,000-space Christiansburg Transit Center at Falling Branch (Exit 118) to the 566-acre New River Vocational Rehabilitation Center & Justin's Station (Exit 98) in Pulaski County.

The Class of '89 & Academic Precedents

CPI is the literal and spiritual birthplace of The Stardust Engine. All five members—Ryan O'Connell, Cassidy O'Connell, Holly O'Connell, Evan Wright, and Tyler Wright—walked across the stage together on The Commonwealth Green as proud graduates of the CPI Class of 1989.

1. The Dual-Enrollment Bridge (1985–1987)

When Ryan (21), Cassidy (19), and twins Evan and Tyler (18) matriculated as CPI freshmen in Fall 1985, youngest sister Holly O'Connell was only 16. Through CPI's joint High School Dual Enrollment partnership with Blacksburg High School, Holly attended morning high-school classes and rode Blue Ridge Transit Route 1 to the CPI campus every afternoon to take 200- and 300-level undergraduate Business Administration and Commercial Contract Law courses. By simultaneously satisfying her Virginia Advanced Studies Diploma and earning two full years of CPI credit, Holly entered CPI full-time as a Junior in Fall 1987 and graduated alongside her siblings and cousins in May 1989.

2. The Summer Session PolyPass Loophole

Under CPI regulations, a student's PolyPass (which turns a CPI student ID into a fare-free unlimited transit pass across Blue Ridge Transit and regional partners) does not normally activate for incoming freshmen until the Fall Semester begins in late August. However, savvy Blacksburg residents—like Jessica, Paige, and Freddie on Pepper Street—discovered that enrolling in a single accelerated Summer Session course (such as Session II: July–August) immediately activates the student's PolyPass upon tuition payment, unlocking two months of free summer mobility across the New River Valley.

The "Forger Nation War Chest" (1992–1995)

The unbreakable bond between CPI alumni and The Stardust Engine saved the band's career after the 1990 highway crash and the 1992 Friction catastrophe. When the family escaped Apex Records with their master tapes intact but their bank accounts drained, CPI students and alumni organized an underground, mail-order grassroots relief drive known as the "Forger Nation War Chest." Tens of thousands of five- and ten-dollar checks mailed in maroon-and-orange envelopes raised the seed capital Holly O'Connell used to incorporate Engine Room Records, LLC and record 1995's The Warehouse Tapes—forever linking the band's independence to the loyalty of Forger Nation.
